title: LoRA: capacity and placement
summary: Two choices shape an adapter: its rank and where you attach it. Follow the connections to see how both affect the adaptation you evaluate.
source: Adapted from the supplied vault's LoRA.md; conceptual example, not an experimental result.

nodes.label: Rank: capacity per adapter
nodes.detail: Rank r sets the size of the low-rank bottleneck. For a weight matrix with dimensions d_out × d_in, an adapter pair has r(d_in + d_out) trainable parameters. Increasing rank adds capacity and cost; it does not guarantee better validation performance.

nodes.label: Targets: where adapters go
nodes.detail: Target selection decides which weight matrices receive adapters. Adding more target matrices creates more trainable adapter pairs. Rank and placement are separate choices.

nodes.label: Base weight W stays frozen
nodes.detail: In standard LoRA fine-tuning, the chosen base weight is kept fixed. The base model still exists; LoRA reduces trainable adaptation parameters rather than automatically shrinking the base model.

nodes.label: Train the low-rank update
nodes.detail: The matrices A and B learn an update ΔW = (α/r)BA under the conventional LoRA scaling. Scaling can vary by implementation. Training changes the adapter parameters while the selected base weights remain frozen.

nodes.label: Combine base and update
nodes.detail: The adapted transformation uses W + ΔW. When supported by the implementation and numerical representation, the update can be merged for inference. Keeping a clean base makes it easier to reuse different adapters.

nodes.label: Evaluate the trade-off
nodes.detail: Compare candidates on suitable validation data and task metrics, along with memory and compute costs. Increase rank or change targets only when the observed benefit justifies it.
